decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Riley says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Riley to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: Who invited that baby?
decisions.situation: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.

result.title: Extremely rude guest
result.body: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

journal.text: I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.

decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Riley points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Riley keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Riley a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Riley asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Riley supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Riley the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Hotel living room
decisions.situation: You ask Riley whether you can camp in the living room. Your packing list contains six cushions and no clothes.

choices.label: Help make a proper sleeping spot

result.title: Room with a sofa
result.body: Riley helps you set up, then checks on you before bed.

journal.text: I camped in the living room with Riley’s help.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Harper wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Harper marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: Glitter lockdown
decisions.situation: You spill a pot of glitter during a class project. Harper finds some inside a closed book.

choices.label: Make a paper funnel for next time

result.title: Still sparkling
result.body: You clean until the bell. There is probably some glitter left in the building forever.

journal.text: I helped clean a classroom after spilling glitter everywhere.

decisions.title: Secrets bingo
decisions.situation: For indoor break, Isla makes bingo cards out of everyone’s embarrassing habits. Your square says “cries at cartoons”. They beg you not to add their baby nickname.

choices.label: Make everyone write their own square
Give a fake sob every time your square comes up
Announce their baby nickname to the room

result.title: Voluntary humiliation
result.body: You admit that cartoon dogs get to you. Someone else confesses to eating a paper cupcake case. Isla quietly removes half the original cards.

journal.text: I turned Isla’s secrets bingo into a game of voluntary confessions.

decisions.title: Is this thing on?
decisions.situation: At assembly rehearsal, Harper asks you to test the microphone. You say “Is this thing on?” The empty hall asks it back.

result.title: Clear enough
result.body: You slow down and read it through. Harper asks you to keep that pace.

journal.text: I practised reading an announcement into the assembly microphone.

decisions.title: The cable is in your hand
decisions.situation: Riley announces that their charger has been missing for three days. You look down. Their charger is in your hand. There is still time to make this worse.

result.title: Found at the scene
result.body: Riley accepts the charger and your apology. Three days of mystery ends in approximately two seconds.

journal.text: I returned Riley’s charger and admitted forgetting about it.

decisions.title: Your signature has improved
decisions.situation: Isla Singh (teacher) thanks you for volunteering to clean the classroom. The roster has your name in Isla Singh (classmate)’s handwriting. Isla Singh (classmate) suddenly becomes interested in the ceiling.

choices.label: Make Isla Singh (classmate) split the work
Walk out and leave Isla Singh (classmate) with it

result.title: A reluctant double act
result.body: Isla Singh (classmate) admits the trick and apologises while stacking chairs. You finish together; Isla Singh (teacher) is glad the room gets done.

journal.text: I made Isla Singh (classmate) share a cleanup they had volunteered me for.

decisions.title: Selective honesty
decisions.situation: Isla has marked a correct answer wrong and a wrong answer right. The mistakes cancel out. You could mention both, or suddenly become very interested in only one.

choices.label: Ask for the lost marks. Hide the free ones.

result.title: No profit, better reputation
result.body: Isla corrects both marks and thanks you for being honest. Your grade stays exactly where it was.

journal.text: I showed Isla two marking mistakes that cancelled each other out.

decisions.title: The unpaid goblin
decisions.situation: Isla Singh (classmate) turns your group presentation into a pitch for an imaginary company. You are listed as “unpaid goblin”. Their dog is CEO. Isla Singh (teacher) asks where the actual research is.

choices.label: Open the real research before the dog gets a salary
Whisper a demand for a better job title
Delete the pitch while they are presenting it

result.title: Goblin saves the meeting
result.body: You present your actual work. Isla Singh (teacher) marks it while Isla Singh (classmate) clicks past a slide about office beanbags. The dog receives no academic credit.

journal.text: I rescued our group presentation after Isla Singh (classmate) replaced the research with a fake company pitch.

decisions.title: Answers attached
decisions.situation: Isla Singh (classmate) sends you a photo of tomorrow’s homework answers. Their message says “delete after reading”, which sounds very normal.

choices.label: Offer to work through it together
Copy it, including the wrong date

result.title: Less convenient
result.body: You work through the questions. You understand the method by the end.

journal.text: I did my own homework after Isla Singh (classmate) sent a photo of the answers.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Melbourne takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Melbourne needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Melbourne.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs A$70.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Melbourne.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Riley also confessed to approving the haircut.
